title: Sold-Out Eden Park Crowd to Break New Zealand Bilateral Record for India T20I
excerpt: Nearly 40,000 fans will watch Friday's fourth T20I in Auckland, passing the 36,523 mark set in 2019 — for a series India have already won.
body:
• Friday's fourth T20I between New Zealand and India at Eden Park is sold out, with nearly 40,000 fans expected in Auckland.
  • The crowd will break New Zealand's bilateral series attendance record of 36,523, set at an Eden Park double-header against India in 2019.
  • It will be the third-largest international cricket crowd in Eden Park's history, behind only the 2015 World Cup semi-final (41,000) and a 1982 ODI against Australia (about 42,000).
  • More than 126,000 tickets have been sold across India's full tour, including over 71,000 for the five-match T20I series alone; India already lead the series 3-0.

New Zealand Cricket has confirmed a complete sell-out for Friday's fourth T20 International against India at Eden Park, a crowd of nearly 40,000 that will set a new bilateral series attendance record and underline the commercial weight India now carry as a touring side. RNZ reported the sell-out as a milestone in sporting ties between the two countries; the fixture is the fourth sell-out of the five-match T20I series, after full houses at Hagley Oval in Christchurch and a pre-sold capacity crowd for Sunday's fifth match at Seddon Park in Hamilton, according to Ministry of Sport.

A record that stood since 2019

The expected crowd passes the previous bilateral mark of 36,523, set at Eden Park in 2019 during a double-header involving the Black Caps, the White Ferns and India. Only two international crowds in the ground's history will remain larger: about 42,000 for a 1982 one-day international against Australia, and 41,000 for the 2015 World Cup semi-final against South Africa, when Grant Elliott's last-over six sent New Zealand into the final. Total ticket sales for the multi-format tour — five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests, titled the Hero VIDA India Tour of New Zealand — have passed 126,000, with more than 71,000 sold for the T20I leg alone.

"There really is nothing like a full house at Eden Park. Breaking a bilateral series attendance record shows just how much appetite there is for this series."

— Glenn Critchley, Chief Marketing and Commercial Officer, New Zealand Cricket

A dead rubber that is not dead at the gate

The striking part is the context. India have already won the series, leading 3-0 after victories in Christchurch and Wellington — the third match was sealed by Abhishek Sharma's 113 off 38 balls as India chased 199 in 13.2 overs. Friday's match cannot change the series result, yet it has drawn the biggest bilateral crowd in New Zealand's history. NZC chief marketing and commercial officer Glenn Critchley said the response had exceeded the board's expectations and that selling out Eden Park was "the cherry on top," as Yardbarker reported. India are aiming for a 4-0 lead on Friday before the series closes in Hamilton on Sunday.

What it says about NZ-India cricket ties

For New Zealand Cricket, a sold-out stadium for a match with nothing riding on it is the clearest possible evidence of what an India tour is worth — in gate receipts, in broadcast value and in the sponsorship the tour carries, led by Indian electric vehicle brand Hero VIDA as title sponsor. For the large Indian diaspora in Auckland, it is also a home crowd in all but name: India's pulling power in New Zealand now fills the country's biggest cricket ground even when the trophy is already decided. Tickets for the ODI and Test legs that follow remain on sale through NZC's official channels.
